findings.title: VIEW permission incorrectly grants global group manage permission
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an FGAP admin granted only the Groups 'view' scope passes the no-arg manage check. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup relies on auth.groups().requireManage(), therefore a view-only admin can create top-level groups and perform other operations gated only by canManage(), a privilege escalation beyond read-only access. canManage() should only accept MANAGE.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2, per-group authorization resources are named with the GroupModel id (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() as the resource name), while Resource.getId() is the authorization-store UUID. This code passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission(), which looks the value up with resourceStore.findByName(), and then adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. Callers such as UsersResource.getUsersCount() and searchForUser() pass that set to user queries as actual group ids, so members of groups the admin may view/manage are miscounted or filtered out, and the specific-group check silently falls back to the all-Groups resource. It should pass and return groupResource.getName().

findings.title: Lazily created resources are not assigned their resource type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource() creates a resource for a known resourceType but never calls resource.setType(resourceType), unlike AdminPermissionsSchema.init() and the V1 permission initializers which explicitly set the type. The new GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() enumerates candidates with resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE), so lazily created per-group resources will not be found by that lookup even after fixing which identifier is returned. The created resource should have its type set to the requested resourceType.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the new Groups type, scopes, or aggregate resource
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore keep a client/resource server created from the old schema: the 'Groups' aggregate resource and group-specific scopes such as manage-members, view-members, and manage-membership are never added. On those realms group permission creation can fail when resolving scopes and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() can dereference a missing Groups type resource, so the new Groups support only works for newly initialized realms unless an upgrade path populates the missing scopes/resources.
